identity.real_world_identity_notes: FIA evidence establishes the S7 competition identity, and specialist technical reporting supports a six-speed sequential transmission in the S7-R family. Exact AMS2 cockpit inspection confirms a sequential stick without paddles.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a round rim without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car stalled when moving from rest without physical clutch input.
All six sequential-stick gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts with automatic throttle cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted and no automatic throttle blip was observed; authentic rev matching therefore requires the driver to blip the throttle manually.
The strongest opened transmission source describes a later S7-R, so exact 2005 historical revision details remain qualified.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Standing-start clutch, six-speed sequential stick without paddles, automatic cut, no automatic blip, and round no-display rim were directly observed.

confidence.basis: Exact simulator identity, modeled hardware, and shift behavior were directly tested; FIA and specialist evidence support the historical car and sequential transmission family while the exact 2005 revision remains qualified.

RaceRoom officially lists Saleen S7R in its GTR 1 class. Saleen's own racing history identifies the S7R as its race version and dates its inaugural competition season to 2001; specialist technical reporting identifies a six-speed sequential S7-R revision introduced in 2002, while a period MotorTrend drive documents an early S7R with a six-speed straight-cut race transmission and short-throw shifter. DailySportscar records the family transition from early H-pattern to later sequential gearboxes. The checked-out repository already contains the compatible curated record saleen-s7-r-gt1, so this observation should join that record rather than create a duplicate.

claims.basis: A first-person drive of the exact early S7R instructs clutch use on both shifts and recommends heel-and-toe on braking downshifts. This supports driver blipping for the family, but does not prove every 2005 Xtrac revision retained the same procedure.
Official release, homologation context, and exact live CarModel/class observation establish the simulated identity.
Specialist family-level evidence and direct exercise of the modeled six-speed sequential stick agree; the historical source is from a later S7-R.
Direct current-game testing and cockpit inspection establish the start clutch, automatic cut, absence of automatic blip, required manual rev matching, and wheel shape.

RSS identifies the exact Shadow implementation, and its installed metadata, American V8 layout, body, specifications, and bundled Saleen and period FIA GT liveries converge on the existing Saleen S7-R GT1 record. The in-game year 2000 is not promoted as a real-car revision because no readable package field declares it and the skins span later seasons.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: The Saleen S7-R, which Assetto Corsa lists as GT Shadow V8. Six-speed sequential, supported by specialist reporting and confirmed in the cockpit as a stick without paddles. The car cuts the upshift; blip every downshift yourself.
